lines.text: I found four works orders under my big book. They say the General Store, Arcade, Post Office and Coffee Cup do not exist.
They have all been standing there very patiently.
Each order has one fault. Four proper signatures will put the buildings back on paper.
The same pen scratched a name from my big book and signed these orders in 1999.
I cannot read the name. It has been scratched with real commitment.
The General Store order is still nailed to its front.
WORKS ORDER. FILED 1999.
GENERAL STORE: CONDEMNED UNTIL 31 FEBRUARY 1999.
February does not have thirty-one days.
STATUS: PENDING.
The date cannot happen.
Thirty-first of February. A date with nowhere to put its coat.
I have corrected the order and signed it.
The General Store boards have come down.
The Arcade order calls its building something else entirely.
WORKS ORDER. FILED 1999.
STRUCTURE: MUNICIPAL WATER TANK.
This is an arcade, not a water tank.
STATUS: CONDEMNED.
The order calls the Arcade a water tank.
A water tank with an arcade written all over it. Paper can be very determined.
I have corrected the building name and signed it.
The Arcade boards have come down.
The Post Office order has put a name where a building should be.
WORKS ORDER. FILED 1999.
CONDEMNED PREMISES: NIB.
Nib is the clerk, not the Post Office.
STATUS: PENDING.
The order names you as the building.
It does. I am flattered, but I am much too small for mail slots.
I have put the Post Office back in its proper space and signed it.
The Post Office boards have come down.
The Coffee Cup order has a signature for the wrong thing.
WORKS ORDER. FILED 1999.
COFFEE CUP: CONDEMNED.
CERTIFIED FOR: FOUNTAIN, CENTRAL SQUARE.
The signature is for the fountain.
The order certifies the fountain instead.
It has condemned coffee and signed for water. That is a full day for one form.
I have signed for the Coffee Cup.
The Coffee Cup boards have come down.
The four-signature certificate is ready at my counter.
Four proper signatures. The four buildings are back in my big book.
I am filing this certificate in the top drawer.
It has a very satisfying square corner.
The old order may remain on its nail. It has earned the fresh air.
